diagnostic.message: Type argument violates upper bound of T
Anonymous override requires an exact inherited method signature
Anonymous supertype arguments cannot be projected
Anonymous override result differs from inherited method
Anonymous generic Unit results require unsupported boxed Unit overrides
Type argument violates upper bound of X
Anonymous enclosing type parameters require an unambiguous emitted lexical declaration
Shadowing an enclosing type parameter is unsupported
Generic, extension, inline, vararg, and defaulted suspend declarations are unsupported

limitations: Concrete generic and nongeneric class and interface bases with constructor substitution, override specialization, erased bridges and JVM generic superclass/interface signatures. Own members must be override functions; anonymous properties, generic methods and covariant bridges remain diagnosed. Superclass default/reordered arguments and conflicting inherited defaults are outside this evidence.

Lexical type variables in anonymous supertypes are covered in generic functions, generic class methods, primary-constructor initializers and generic interface default methods, with EnclosingMethod/InnerClasses and reflective generic declarations, override signatures and captures. Anonymous Kotlin metadata and full anonymous identity in exported APIs remain outside this evidence. Shadowed method/class type-variable names, generic suspend contexts, ordinary-lambda enclosing contexts remain explicit unsupported boundaries.
Java callers compile once against official Kotlin output, then execute unchanged with verification against both providers.
